title: Unified Inference Product Hub: PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release - 2027-04
author: Sofia Chen
summary: Product hub covering the Unified Inference product: consolidated product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap & themes for the next 12 months, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the 2027-04 milestone.
overview: Purpose: Provide a single source-of-truth for the Unified Inference product family (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) to align engineering, GTM, and customer success on scope, priorities, and launch criteria. This document consolidates the product overview, PRD requirements, design constraints, roadmap & themes, pricing guidance, and release notes for the April 2027 milestone.
goals:
1) Make it easy for engineering and product teams to find requirements and ownership for Unified Inference features.
2) Surface roadmap themes and release prioritization for the next 12 months.
3) Provide pricing and packaging guidance for sales and finance.
4) Record release notes and launch checklist for the 2027-04 release.
key_features:
- Unified API surface supporting text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- Smart routing across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with policy-driven fallbacks.
- Cost-aware runtime controls (batching, caching, quantization profiles).
- Observability and rollout tooling in Redwood Console (per-model dashboards, trace hooks, error analysis).
- Private deployment support with VPC and KMS/HSM integrations.
requirements:
MUST requirements (v1):
1) API parity: New 'unify.v1' endpoint must support text, chat, embeddings, and function/tool calling.
2) Backwards compatible model routing: requests using legacy endpoints must be routed to compatible model variants automatically.
3) SLA targets: 99.9% availability for hosted API; P99 latency targets of <= 250ms for short responses (<=128 tokens) on standard SKU.
4) Security: Support per-customer KMS key binding for Private deployments and audit logging of model selection decisions.
5) Observability: Token-level cost and latency breakdowns available in Console for each route.
6) Billing: Accurate per-token and per-embedding metering with monthly export to billing pipeline.

Optional / Nice-to-have:
- Adaptive quantization profiles per workload class.
- Automated model regression detection tied to prompt sets.

Requirements matrix (example):
| Requirement ID | Description | Priority | Owner |
| RQ-001 | unify.v1 API surface (text/chat/embeddings) | Must | Product/Eng-API |
| RQ-002 | Smart routing with fallback policies | Must | Eng-Platform |
| RQ-003 | Per-route Console metrics and traces | Must | Eng-Platform/Observability |
| RQ-004 | Dedicated autoscaling policy integration | High | Eng-Infrastructure |
| RQ-005 | Private KMS/HSM integration and audit logs | High | Security/Eng-Private |
design_specifications:
Design principles:
- Backwards compatibility: migration must be transparent for existing customers.
- Predictable economics: provide knobs that map to clear unit cost impacts.
- Observability-first: every routing decision and quantization fallback must be visible in the Console.

High-level architecture:
- API Gateway (unify.v1) receives requests -> Auth & routing -> Policy Engine -> Router selects target pool (hosted / dedicated / private) -> Runtime Executor (batching + KV cache + quantization profile) -> Token streaming back to client.

Components & responsibilities:
- Policy Engine: evaluates tenant policy (latency_class, cost_budget, region) and selects routing candidates. Must expose a deterministic decision log.
- Router: maintains model catalog and compatibility matrix; supports graceful fallback to model variants when primary is unavailable.
- Runtime Executor: GPU-optimized inference engine with continuous batching and KV cache; supports per-tenant quantization profile and prefix cache.

Data contracts & APIs (examples):
- unify.v1 POST /generate {
  "model": "string",
  "input": "string",
  "route_policy": {"latency_class":"low|medium|high", "cost_priority":"economy|balanced|quality"},
  "trace_id": "string"
}

- Policy decision log schema (flattened fields for audit): tenant_id, request_id, decision_timestamp, selected_pool, selected_model, fallback_reason, estimated_cost_tokens

Performance targets & constraints:
- P50 token generation latency <= 40ms on optimized SKU for 8k context with continuous batching.
- Memory: runtime must support 100k KV cache entries per node with eviction policy LRU per-tenant.

Compatibility & migration plan:
1) Launch unify.v1 in parallel with legacy endpoints for 6 weeks.
2) Route 10% of traffic gradually for early telemetry, increase to 50% after 2 weeks if no regressions.
3) Communicate breaking changes to customers 30 days before deprecation windows.
roadmap_and_themes:
Roadmap themes (12-month view):
- Theme A (Q2-Q3 2027): Stability & SLA maturity - focus on P99 reductions, SRE runbooks, and Dedicated autoscaling improvements.
- Theme B (Q3-Q4 2027): Cost optimization - rollout Redwood Optimize v7 recommendations integrated into Console with one-click profiles.
- Theme C (Q4 2027 - Q1 2028): Private deployment parity - KMS/HSM, on-prem packaging, and hardened network controls.
- Theme D (Q1 2028): Developer ergonomics - SDK updates, improved streaming semantics, and structured output tooling.

Planned milestones (next 6 months):
- 2027-04: unify.v1 GA (hosted) + Console metrics for per-route breakdowns.
- 2027-06: Dedicated autoscaling policy release + initial Optimize v7 integrations.
- 2027-09: Private KMS binding beta and onprem packaging alpha.
- 2027-11: Cost monitoring + one-click Optimize profiles GA.

Prioritization rationale:
- Stability & SLAs prioritized to reduce churn and support enterprise expansion.
- Cost controls follow to improve unit economics and lower time-to-value for customers.
- Private parity prioritized for regulated customers and net-new enterprise deals.
pricing_and_packaging:
Pricing principles:
- Transparent unit economics: separate per-token generation, per-embedding, and reserved capacity charges.
- Match price to performance tier: premium for low-latency optimized SKUs, discounted for dedicated reserved capacity.

Suggested packaging (example):
- Self-serve Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation price (e.g., $0.0012 / 1k tokens for balanced models), per-embedding price ($0.0008 / embedding). Includes Console access and basic SLOs.
- Dedicated (committed monthly): base reservation + usage overage. Tiers: small (8 GPUs), medium (32 GPUs), large (128 GPUs) with discounts of 25-40% vs hosted on committed spend.
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + deployment support + optional onprem license. Includes advanced compliance add-ons (audit retention, HSM).

Add-ons & discounts:
- Advanced observability retention (90 days): additional monthly fee.
- Premium SLA & support: enterprise add-on for 24/7 response and faster remediation.
- Volume discounts: stepped pricing at 1M, 10M, 100M tokens per month.
release_notes:
Release: Unified Inference GA - 2027-04-12 (v1.0)
Highlights:
- GA of unify.v1 API supporting text, chat, embeddings, and function/tool calling.
- Per-route Console metrics (latency, cost, token breakdowns) and trace hooks.
- Smart routing with deterministic decision logs and automatic fallback to model variants.
- Dedicated autoscaling policies (beta) integrated with the Capacity Planner.

Fixes and improvements:
- Reduced cold-start latency for common model families by ~18% via kernel prewarm.
- Resolved edge-case where KV cache eviction could cause stale prefix reads under high churn.

Known issues & workarounds:
- KISS-1423: Private KMS binding does not yet support asymmetric HSM keys in the current beta. Workaround: use customer-managed symmetric keys and rotate per policy.
- PERF-887: P99 latency on extremely long generation requests (>16k tokens) can spike; recommend configuring `latency_class: high` to route to high-memory optimized SKUs.

Telemetry & KPIs to monitor post-release:
- Adoption: percentage of active customers calling unify.v1 vs legacy endpoints. Target 50% within 6 weeks.
- Stability: SLO compliance (99.9% uptime) and P99 latency for short responses.
- Cost: average cost per 1k tokens across top 25 tenants.
